card.name: How and with what to give a remedy
card.fires_on: Words just before an instruction on how a treatment should be given or taken, such as 'should be given', 'Milk or' antacids, or 'slow' infusion of protamine. Seen in overdose, reversal and stomach-irritation advice.

modes.label: Be given / taken
modes.description: The verb given or taken in a passive instruction about administering a drug, often with conditions.
modes.example: it is recommended that doxycycline be<< given>> with food or milk.

modes.label: Antidote or soothing agent
modes.description: The word or joining milk to antacids as agents to be given after overdose.
modes.example: Milk<< or>> antacids should be given to bind

modes.label: Slow protamine infusion
modes.description: The word slow before intravenous protamine used to neutralize heparin.
modes.example: protamine sulfate (1% solution) by<< slow>> infusion will neutralize heparin sodium
